title: Signed-in readers and the author comment and reply at any depth under a report, in plain text with GitHub name and avatar; the author's posts carry an 'Author' badge
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1: A signed-in reader (the author included, through the same form) posts a comment on a published report; signed-out visitors cannot post: missing
C2: Comment text is plain text, shown as literal text, never interpreted as HTML: missing
C3: Each comment is shown publicly under the report with the poster's GitHub name and avatar: missing
C4: A reply can be posted under any comment or reply, at any depth (tree of any depth): missing
C5: Top-level comments are listed oldest first, each with its replies indented beneath it: missing
C6: A removed or blocked comment with visible replies below it (at any depth) shows a 'comment removed' placeholder; one with nothing visible below it disappears entirely: missing
C7: A comment whose GitHub user ID equals the pinned owner ID carries an 'Author' badge next to the name: missing

Where the badge is computed. practice: inside comments.Tree, with an ownerID argument and Node.ByOwner. crossdomain: in internal/server's buildThread, from Node.GitHubID. Taken: crossdomain, which keeps internal/comments free of auth and config.
The 'no usable target' error is named ErrNoTarget (crossdomain) rather than ErrNotOpen (practice). The votes name means 'no published report', and this error also covers parents.
Post's argument order is (reportID, githubID, parentID, body), matching votes.Cast, rather than practice's (reportID, parentID, githubID, body).

Template files. The defines-only templates/comments.html (practice) holds the section and the recursive comment block. crossdomain put the section in report.html and the comment block in thread.html. SC-013's page is branch.html.
Placeholder wording: 'comment removed' (practice, the brief's own words) rather than 'Comment removed'. Class names: removed and cut rather than removed-note and cut-note.
SC-013's branch page and redirect use Tree plus a pure Find (crossdomain) rather than new Branch and Ancestry SQL with a recursive CTE (practice).

attempts.head: 93e28aadd9a7c2538cf0b3067ce451d570a14cba
attempts.summary: Both proposals agree on most of the shape, and that shape matches the code as it stands: - an adjacency-list `comments` table keyed to reports.id; - single-statement INSERT…SELECT writes that copy votes.Cast; - a handler that follows vote.go step by step and answers through auth.SeeOther; - one flat id-ordered read, pruned bottom-up in Go; - a recursive html/template block drawn by renderReader, so the thread shows on both / and /reports/<slug>; - the badge worked out at render time from auth.IsOwner; - a server-side depth cap that respects the measured Chrome no-go.

attempts.summary: The two proposals were written after spike 197 and agree on everything load-bearing.

caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 2 forks that only a measurement can settle. O-016: unsettled design fork: Does deleting a report remove all of its comments, at any reply-chain depth, under the self-FK action chosen? Specifically: with the composite parent FK as NO ACTION and report_id ON DELETE CASCADE, does `DELETE FROM reports WHERE id = ?` succeed on a report holding a reply chain 1,500 deep, and leave 0 comment rows? Its context: Both proposals put ON DELETE CASCADE on the self-FK. The synthesis uses NO ACTION, because a cascade through parent links may hit SQLite's trigger-depth limit (recalled), and relies on NO ACTION being checked at the end of the statement (recalled). The build settles it with TestDeleteReportWithDeepChain before the migration is final. If NO ACTION fails, the alternative is CASCADE, with that same deep-chain test proving it does not hit the depth limit. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: Measure this in the risk spike. Do not leave it to the build. HOW TO MEASURE Work in a fresh clone of the repo at 93e28aa, not the SL-006 worktree. Set TAAD3_HOME to a new empty scratch folder, use a scratch GOCACHE, and set GOTOOLCHAIN=local and GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly, so the modernc.org/sqlite version is the one go.mod pins. Add a scratch migration 0004 holding the design's exact DDL: - comments STRICT: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT; report_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES reports(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; parent_id INTEGER; github_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(github_id); body TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(body)>0); created_at INTEGER NOT NULL; removed_at INTEGER; UNIQUE(report_id,id); FOREIGN KEY(report_id,parent_id) REFERENCES comments(report_id,id). - blocked_accounts. - comments_children ON comments(report_id,parent_id). Open the database through store.Open, so the real migrate.go applies it and the serving-pool pragmas are in force. Assert PRAGMA foreign_keys = 1 on that pool. Seed: - report A with one reply chain 1,500 deep; - report B with a second chain 10,000 deep; - report C with a few comments whose ids are interleaved with A's; - a vote on A. Delete A through the product's own path: reports.Library.Delete, or failing that the same `DELETE FROM reports WHERE id = ?` on the serving pool. Then delete B the same way. RECORD - the error, if any, with its exact text; - comment rows left for A and for B (must be 0); - C's comment count (must be unchanged); - A's vote rows (must be 0); - the time each delete took. CONTROL, so that 0 rows cannot come from an FK that does nothing: a single `DELETE FROM comments WHERE id = <a comment on C that has a reply>` must fail with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed. IN THE SAME RUN, measure the fallback the same way, so a NO ACTION failure does not cost a second lap. That fallback is the composite self-FK declared DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED. It is not CASCADE: critique m3 / O-020 dropped CASCADE. HOW THE RESULT DECIDES THE FORK 1. NO ACTION: if both deletes return nil, leave 0 rows for A and B, leave C intact, and the control fails as expected, NO ACTION stays as designed. No re-synthesis. 2. DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED: if NO ACTION errors or leaves rows, and the deferred variant passes the same checks, the schema uses DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED and the design is rewritten with that. 3. If both fail, the design is rewritten with that result. It then needs a delete that does not depend on the parent-FK action, and the synthesist must design it. TestDeleteReportWithDeepChain stays as the build's regression case (O-010). It checks the answer measured here and does not decide it. The question is about what SQLite does, and it can be answered on this machine in seconds. Nothing has measured it yet: - The three spikes measured finish-test shape, report-id stability and Chrome DOM depth. - The replace spike's scratch_child had only a single-column FK to reports, with no self-FK. - The critique confirmed end-of-statement checking from sqlite.org text, and the trigger-depth failure from another project's PR. Both are cited, not run under this repo's modernc.org/sqlite and pragmas. The design wants the build to settle it with a test 'before the migration is final'. That is the case the brief warns about: a builder settles the fork by writing code, and no decision is recorded. The fork's own context still names CASCADE as the fallback. Accepted finding m3 (O-020) replaced CASCADE with DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, so the measurement compares NO ACTION with that variant. Measuring both variants in one run uses one of the two laps allowed and leaves the second spare. The 10,000-deep chain covers the 'any depth' wording and costs nothing extra: a few MB in a temp dir. Running it through the real store.Open pool and Library.Delete means the result is about the product's delete path, not a toy connection. O-017: unsettled design fork: Under modernc.org/sqlite, does the composite FK (report_id, parent_id) → comments(report_id, id) with UNIQUE(report_id, id) accept NULL-parent rows and refuse a raw cross-report reply? Its context: Both proposals recall that it does. If it does not, the schema drops the composite FK and keeps only Post's EXISTS as the guard, which changes the data model. Settled by TestSchema in internal/comments. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: Measure this in the risk spike, in the same run and scratch clone as O-016: the same 0004 DDL, applied through the real store.Open and migrate.go (foreign keys off, then PRAGMA foreign_key_check), with the pinned modernc.org/sqlite. Use two published reports, A and B, and one user. Every statement below is raw SQL on the serving pool, with PRAGMA foreign_keys = 1 asserted first. WHAT TO RUN, AND WHAT EACH SHOULD GIVE (a) INSERT a comment on A with parent_id NULL. Must succeed. (b) INSERT a reply on A whose parent_id is (a)'s id. Must succeed. (c) INSERT a row with report_id = B and parent_id = (a)'s id (a raw cross-report reply). Must fail with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed, extended code SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY (787). (d) INSERT on A with a parent_id that no row has. Must fail the same way. (e) PRAGMA foreign_key_check(comments) after (a) and (b). Must return 0 rows and must not raise 'foreign key mismatch'. (f) The migration itself must apply without error and set user_version 4. Record the exact error text for (c) and (d), and the row counts after each step. HOW THE RESULT DECIDES THE FORK - All of (a)-(f) as stated: the composite FK backed by UNIQUE(report_id, id) stays exactly as designed. No re-synthesis. - If (a) fails, (c) succeeds, or any step raises 'foreign key mismatch': the design is rewritten without the composite FK. parent_id becomes a plain INTEGER, Post's EXISTS (same report, visible parent) is the only guard, and the 'raw SQL insert with a cross-report parent' shape comes out of case 5. TestSchema in internal/comments stays as the build's regression case (O-005). It checks the answer measured here and does not decide it. The composite FK is an expensive-to-reverse part of the data model: adding or dropping it later needs a table rebuild through the hot migrate.go (lesson #930). Both proposals and the synthesis list its NULL-skip and cross-report refusal as 'recalled'. No spike or command has run them under modernc.org/sqlite. A mistake in how the FK is declared, such as a parent key not exactly covered by a unique index, shows up only at DML time as 'foreign key mismatch', not when the table is created. Only running inserts against the real schema can rule it out. The design wants TestSchema in the build to settle it, which again leaves the build to decide a data-model fork by writing code. The check is cheap, a handful of inserts in a temp DB, and it runs in the same spike run and scratch clone as O-016. Together the two forks use one lap of the two allowed. The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.
